title: Koszul-at-a-point equivalence under arbitrary parameter base change for flat scheme families
statement: Let $B,X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $p:X\to B$, $q:Y\to B$ and $f:X\to Y$ satisfy $qf=p$. Assume $p$ and $q$ are flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A scheme morphism is lci if, locally on its source, it factors as a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose ideal is locally generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence], followed by a smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; the empty sequence is allowed. It is Koszul at a point if its restriction to some open neighbourhood of that point is lci. For every scheme morphism $g:T\to B$, form $X_T=X\times_BT$, $Y_T=Y\times_BT$ and $f_T:X_T\to Y_T$ using [def-pc-fibre-product], and write $\pi:X_T\to X$ for the projection. For every $x_T\in X_T$, the morphism $f_T$ is Koszul at $x_T$ if and only if $f$ is Koszul at $\pi(x_T)$. There is no flatness assumption on $g$ or on $f$, and no separation, quasi-compactness, Noetherian, or nonemptiness assumption.

source.place: Tag 06B8 (lemma-base-change-lci-fibres), pointwise meaning of the base-change equality; lci and Koszul-at-a-point conventions in definition-lci.

proof.text: Fix $x_T$ and write $x=\pi(x_T)$, $b=p(x)$ and $t\in T$ for its parameter image. The local-finite-presentation cancellation lemma [lem-a1-map-over-base-finite-presentation] applies to $X\to Y\to B$: $p$ is locally finitely presented and $q$ is locally of finite type since it is locally finitely presented. Choose affine neighbourhoods $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $b$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $f(x)$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}C$ of $x$, with $U\subset f^{-1}V$ and $V\subset q^{-1}W$, on which $A$ is finitely presented over $R$ and $C$ finitely presented over $A$; principal refinements preserve these presentations. A presentation $C=A[z_1,\ldots,z_n]/I$ gives a closed immersion $i:U\hookrightarrow P=\mathbf A^n_V$ with finitely generated ideal $I$. The projection $P\to V$ is smooth [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], and so is its composite $P\to Y$ by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](b). The polynomial projection is flat [lem-nagata-polynomial-projection-flat], so $P\to W$ is flat by [lem-pc-flat-compose]. It is finitely presented: adjoining the $z_j$ to a finite presentation of $A$ over $R$ gives a finite presentation of $A[z]$ over $R$. Both $U\to W$ and $V\to W$ are flat by the original hypotheses; restriction does not change their local rings. The affine flatness criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] therefore makes $R\to C$ and $R\to A[z]$ flat.

source.place: Tag 06B8 (lemma-base-change-lci-fibres), local polynomial factorization; Tag 02FV in morphisms.tex. The affine presentation is written out.

proof.text: Suppose $f$ is Koszul at $x$. Restrict its defining smooth factorization and the polynomial factorization of step 1 to a common source neighbourhood. By [lem-sfb-koszul-immersion-smooth-ambient-independence], $i$ is Koszul-regular there. A Koszul-regular sequence is $H_1$-regular by [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Its source is flat over $W$ and its ambient scheme is locally finitely presented over $W$, so [lem-sfb-relative-h1-immersion-universal-koszul] makes $i_T$ Koszul-regular near $x_T$ for the arbitrary map $T\times_BW\to W$. The pullbacks of $U$ and $V$ are open neighbourhoods of the relevant points by [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product]. Smooth base change [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2) makes the pulled-back projection $P_T\to V_T$ smooth. Its composite with the open inclusion $V_T\subset Y_T$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](b). Thus this is the defining lci factorization of $f_T$ near $x_T$.

source.place: Tag 06B8, preservation direction, supplied explicitly by divisors.tex Tag 063V (lemma-flat-relative-H1-regular), (2).

proof.text: Conversely suppose $f_T$ is Koszul at $x_T$. The base change $P_T\to Y_T$ of the smooth map $P\to Y$ is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). Ambient independence [lem-sfb-koszul-immersion-smooth-ambient-independence], applied on a common source neighbourhood to this chart and the defining lci chart of $f_T$, makes $i_T$ Koszul-regular near $x_T$. The morphism $U_T\to T\times_BW$ is flat by [lem-sfb-pointwise-flatness-base-change](1), and $P_T\to T\times_BW$ is locally finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Apply [lem-sfb-relative-h1-immersion-universal-koszul] to a source neighbourhood on which $i_T$ is Koszul-regular; the $H_1$ condition follows from [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Base change to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ gives a Koszul-regular immersion $(i_T)_t$ near the fibre point represented by $x_T$. This avoids assuming the parameter map $g$ is flat.

source.place: Tag 06B8, proof through the fibre immersion at t; Tag 063V upgrades its H1 conclusion to Koszul regularity.

proof.text: The canonical fibre comparison [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change] identifies $(i_T)_t$ with the base change of $i_b:U_b\to P_b$ along the induced field extension $\kappa(b)\to\kappa(t)$, compatibly with the fibre point above $x$; both closed subschemes have the pulled-back defining equations. Here $P_b$ is locally of finite type over $\kappa(b)$ because $A[z]$ is finitely presented over $R$. Therefore [lem-sfb-field-extension-immersion-koszul-points] reflects the conclusion of step 3: $i_b$ is Koszul-regular near $x$, regarded as a point of $U_b$.

source.place: Tag 06B8, residue-field descent paragraph using descent.tex Tag 0694.

proof.text: Put $D=A[z_1,\ldots,z_n]$ and $F=D\otimes_R\kappa(b)$. Let $Q\subset D$ be the prime corresponding to $i(x)$ and $Q_b\subset F$ the corresponding fibre prime. By [lem-sfb-koszul-closed-immersion-affine-criterion], step 4 gives, locally around $Q_b$, generators of $IF$ which are Koszul-regular; their germs generate $IF_{Q_b}$ and remain Koszul-regular. The same criterion expresses the sheaf condition by germs, so this does not require choosing one set of generators over the whole fibre. The ring $F$ is a finite type algebra over the field $\kappa(b)$ and hence Noetherian by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]. Its localization $F_{Q_b}$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] and is nonzero local. Each generator lies in its maximal ideal because $x\in U_b$. Thus [lem-per-noetherian-local-koszul-criterion] makes these germs a regular sequence, including the empty-list case. Consequently $IF_{Q_b}$ is generated by a regular sequence.

source.place: Tag 06B8, last paragraph, with divisors.tex Tag 063W (lemma-fibre-quasi-regular), (2); here the Noetherian fibre conversion is explicit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-flat-quotient-fiber-regular-sequence] to $R\to D$, the finitely generated presentation ideal $I$, and the primes corresponding to $b$, $i(x)$ and its fibre point. All its hypotheses hold: $D$ is flat and finitely presented over $R$ by step 1, $D/I=C$ is flat over $R$ by step 1, and the fibre-local ideal is regular by step 5. Obtain $h\notin Q$ such that $ID[1/h]$ is generated by a regular sequence. It is Koszul-regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular]. The principal affine criterion [lem-sfb-koszul-closed-immersion-affine-criterion] therefore makes $i$ Koszul-regular near $x$. Finally restrict the smooth projection $P\to V$ to this principal ambient open, then compose with $V\hookrightarrow Y$, using [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](a),(b). The resulting factorization is the defining lci factorization for $f$ on a neighbourhood of $x$. This proves reflection and hence the asserted equivalence at every $x_T$. If $X_T$ is empty there is no point to check. No nonemptiness or separation was used.

source.place: Tag 06B8, final application of divisors.tex Tag 063W (lemma-fibre-quasi-regular), (2), in its existing affine form.

lean.statement: theorem scheme_relative_lci_base_change_points {B X Y : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ B) (q : Y ⟶ B) (f : X ⟶ Y) (h : p = f ≫ q) [Flat p] [Flat q] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation p] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation q] {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ B) (xT : (pullback p g : Scheme.{u})) : (∃ U : (pullback p g).Opens, xT ∈ U ∧ RelativeFiniteHilbert.SchemeLci (U.ι ≫ pullback.map p g q g f (𝟙 T) (𝟙 B) ((Category.comp_id p).trans h) ((Category.comp_id g).trans (Category.id_comp g).symm))) ↔ ∃ V : X.Opens, (pullback.fst p g) xT ∈ V ∧ RelativeFiniteHilbert.SchemeLci (V.ι ≫ f)
